Subject: Renewal discussion — capping rate increases with multi-year prepay

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well. As we’re approaching our renewal window for Q1 2027, Procurement is exploring a multi-year prepay structure to lock unit pricing and reduce exposure to year-over-year increases.

High level: Acme wants a 3-year commitment (2027–2029) with an annualized ramp (we expect usage to grow ~40% year 1, 20% year 2). Our primary ask: a firm per-token rate cap for the term and an agreed annual true-up (usage vs committed).

Could you share what Redwood can offer on a multi-year prepay (discounts by committed tier, ramp schedule, and any protection clauses for pricing increases)? We’re aiming to finalize commercial terms by the end of October.

Thanks — looping in Sarah from our side for procurement details.

Cheers,
Oliver King
Contracts Manager
Acme Corp

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capping rate increases with multi-year prepay

Hi Oliver / Sarah —

Appreciate the clarity on timeline and growth expectations. Attached is a first-pass "Rate Assurance" term sheet that aims to address your asks. Key elements summarized below:

- Commitment: 3-year prepay (2027–2029) paid annually in advance or via scheduled invoices.
- Ramp schedule: tiered commit buckets (Year 1: 40% of expected annual usage committed, Year 2: +20%, Year 3: +10% incremental) with a 90-day notice window for major deviations.
- Rate assurance: fixed per-token cap for the contract term (no upward pricing adjustments from Redwood for covered units).
- Discounts: volume-based discounts applied at each annual true-up (examples in attached sheet).
- Annual true-up: reconcile actual usage against committed amounts; overages billed at a capped overage rate.
- Protection clauses: inflation indexing only permitted in narrow circumstances (e.g., material cloud cost changes) with 60-day notice and review with Acme.

I’ve attached ACME-Rate-Assurance-TermSheet-v1.pdf with example numbers and a short appendix on how the annual true-up works operationally.

Next steps: if this looks directionally good, I’ll run the numbers with Rishi and Marissa to firm up discounts and finalize a DocuSign-ready agreement.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ACME Rate Assurance - discount ladder suggestions (internal)

Mina / Marissa —

Quick internal note before we send the updated term sheet to Acme:

- Recommend tightening the Year 1 discount to protect economics if they undercommit (move floor to 12% at Y1 committed volume).
- For Year 2 and Year 3, propose a step-down discount ladder (18% -> 15%) tied to cumulative committed spend, not just incremental.
- Add an "annual inflation cap" clause — max 3% upward adjustment to instantiated non-token fees (not unit token price) if cloud costs move dramatically.
- Keep the rate cap language explicit: "covered units" must be defined as token consumption for API calls excluding embeddings for model X.

If Mina is comfortable with those, I can pre-approve the numbers and we can send v2 to Acme with a suggested DocuSign envelope.

-Rishi
V.P., Sales — Redwood Inference

- Defined covered units and excluded embedding workloads for model-legacy-embedding.
- Annual true-up process clarified: 30-day reconciliation window after each contract year; overages billed at the agreed capped overage rate.
- Added 3% cap on non-token fee inflation triggers (cloud pass-through scenarios).

Attached: ACME-Rate-Assurance-TermSheet-v2.pdf. If this aligns, please sign the bundled agreement via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABC-DF-ACME-2026
